name: Southern Company

summary.text: Southern Company is an Atlanta-based holding company that, according to its SEC filings, owns all of the common stock of three regulated electric utilities (Alabama Power, Georgia Power and Mississippi Power), Southern Power Company and Southern Company Gas, a natural gas distributor in four states. Its chief executive Thomas Fanning is a past chairman of the Edison Electric Institute. Documents obtained by Greenpeace under freedom of information law and reported in 2015 showed Southern Company Services paid about $409,000 between 2006 and 2015 for research by Smithsonian scientist Willie Soon under contracts that gave the company advance review of publications and barred identifying it as a funder without consent. Southern's subsidiary Mississippi Power abandoned the coal gasifier at its Kemper County plant in 2017, writing off about $6.4 billion; related shareholder derivative suits were settled in 2022 with governance reforms.

facts.claim: Southern Company's Form 10-K describes it as a holding company that owns all of the outstanding common stock of three traditional electric operating companies (Alabama Power, Georgia Power and Mississippi Power), Southern Power Company and Southern Company Gas. Other subsidiaries include Southern Nuclear, which operates the system's nuclear plants, and PowerSecure. The 10-K is filed jointly by the parent and its principal subsidiaries.
facts.quote: Southern Company is a holding company that owns all of the outstanding common stock of three traditional electric operating companies, Southern Power Company, and Southern Company Gas.

facts.claim: Southern Company completed the sale of its Florida utility Gulf Power to NextEra Energy on 1 January 2019 for approximately $5.8 billion in cash, less assumed debt.
facts.quote: Southern Company completed its sale of Gulf Power to NextEra Energy for an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $5.8 billion

facts.claim: Inside Climate News reported in February 2015, based on documents obtained by Greenpeace and the Climate Investigations Center, that Southern Company Services gave research grants totalling $409,754 between 2006 and 2015 to Smithsonian scientist Willie Soon. The Smithsonian contracts provided Southern with an advance written copy of proposed publications for comment and barred the Smithsonian from identifying Southern as a funder without the company's written consent. Soon described his papers as 'deliverables' in correspondence with funders.
facts.quote: The contracts also say the Smithsonian will provide Southern Company with "an advance written copy of proposed publications regarding the deliverables for comment and input, if any".

facts.claim: Southern Company publicly opposed the EPA's proposed Clean Power Plan, with CEO Tom Fanning calling the proposed emission guidelines unworkable and urging the EPA to withdraw them; the company said the rule could cost $1 trillion to implement. Fanning later said his challenge had been about federal overreach into state jurisdiction rather than carbon.
facts.quote: "My challenge on [the CPP] had nothing to do with carbon, and had everything to do with federal overreach from a regulatory body on what is otherwise a state purview," said Fanning.

facts.claim: Mississippi Power's Kemper County plant, a coal gasification project with a reported total cost of about $7.5 billion, halted gasifier operations in 2017 and was converted to run on natural gas, with the company writing off about $6.4 billion. On 1 December 2017 Mississippi Power announced a settlement with the Mississippi Public Service Commission and other parties over the remaining Kemper costs, which regulators later approved.
facts.quote: Mississippi Power eventually halted gasifier operations in 2017 and canceled the project, forcing the company to write off $6.4 billion in expenses.

facts.claim: Shareholder derivative suits alleging that Southern Company's directors and officers caused the company to make false or misleading statements about the Kemper project's cost and schedule were settled in 2022. The settlement provided for corporate governance changes rather than payments to individuals, with Southern paying plaintiffs' attorney fees. The settlement notice stated that plaintiffs contended the alleged breaches had exposed the company to a related securities class action and to a continuing U.S. Department of Justice investigation.
facts.quote: According to the notice, the Settlement will result in changes to the Company's corporate governance, not in payments to individuals.

connections.claim: Southern Company Services provided research grants totalling about $409,754 between 2006 and 2015 for Willie Soon's work at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics, under contracts that gave the company advance review of publications and required its consent before it was identified as a funder.
connections.quote: Inside Climate News gave a slightly different number, citing research grants from Southern Co. totaling $409,754 between 2006 and 2015.

connections.claim: Southern Company's research funding for Willie Soon was channelled through contracts with the Smithsonian, which agreed to give Southern advance copies of proposed publications and not to identify Southern as a funder without its written consent.
connections.quote: Under the publicity clause, the Smithsonian agreed that it would "not publish and utilize the name or otherwise identify" Southern Company or its affiliates as a funder of Soon's research without the company's written consent.

connections.claim: Southern Company CEO Thomas Fanning is a past chairman of the Edison Electric Institute, the trade association of investor-owned electric utilities.
connections.quote: He is also a past chairman of the Conference of Chairs of the Federal Reserve Banks and the Edison Electric Institute (EEI).

sources.title: Fanning receives EEI Distinguished Leadership Award

openQuestions: Southern Company's membership of the Global Climate Coalition could not be sourced from the material found.
Southern Company's role in drafting the 1998 API communications plan and in the Soon funding total is already recorded in the API findings and was not repeated.
Whether an SEC investigation of Kemper existed was not established; the derivative settlement filing refers to a continuing Department of Justice investigation.
The year of Fanning's EEI chairmanship and the date of the Clean Power Plan statements were not confirmed from the sources found.
